sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 closed at 7,551.81 on Sep 16, its lowest close of the past month, down three straight sessions from 7,656.98 on Sep 11. The Nasdaq 100 sits at 28,945.06, within a fraction of a percent of its own 1-month low. The Euro Stoxx 50 has drifted the same way, closing at 6,266.50, just above its 1-month floor of 6,236.50. The VIX has ticked up to 17.71, close to its 1-month high of 17.84 — consistent with a slow grind lower rather than a sharp dislocation. Six operating names in the tracked universe report this week, split across consumer (AZO, THO, GIS, COST), industrials (CTAS) and technology (SNX).

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Tue: AZO US and THO US both report into the consumer-cyclical group, which has traded close to flat this cycle (-0.15% median reaction across 497 tickers). Wed: CTAS US reports into industrials, the softest reactor of the sectors touched this week at -1.46% median across 604 tickers, the same day GIS US reports into consumer-defensive (-0.56% median, 362 tickers). Thu: COST US also reports into consumer-defensive alongside GIS's sector read, while SNX US reports into technology — the only one of this week's four sectors with a positive median reaction, at +0.87% across 567 tickers.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the sector reaction table this cycle at +6.62% median across 172 tickers, backed by a thick news window (2,630 items) — the highest-conviction read on the board. Alternative-asset-management (+2.93%, 6 tickers, 232 items) and copper (+2.63%, 6 tickers, 248 items) follow but run on much thinner news coverage. None of this week's six reporters sit in these three groups, so the strongest sector tailwind on the board doesn't touch this week's calendar directly.
